note: Every public claim of the README, with its evidence and the test that keeps it honest. Status: established (evidence recorded and tested), under_validation (pre-registered, runs in progress), not_established (not claimed). tests/test_claims.py fails if recorded evidence stops supporting an established claim.

claims.statement: adds_information is true exactly when the permutation p-value is below 0.05 and the increment is above 0
Items sharing a group never sit in both the training and the test fold
The verdict does not change under monotone rescaling of the score
--fast keeps the false-flag rate at or below 0.10 on every registered no-signal scenario (nominal 0.05)
--fast detects moderate and strong planted signal in at least 80% of runs
On real detectors the tool reproduces seven independent prior analyses (verdict, magnitude within the prior interval widened by 0.02, ordering)
On real data structures with the detector replaced by a no-information one, every false-flag rate is at most 0.10
Editing any file in an evidence package, or removing or reordering a ledger entry, is detected by verify-evidence
The package opens no network connection
The binary engine's output is fixed to 1e-12 for a given version and pinned dependencies
A policy cannot invoke an uncalibrated rule (minimum gain, other alpha, other metric)
The 0.12 null keeps interaction-only detectors at or below 0.10 false flags (upper 95% bound)

The increment's 95% clustered DeLong interval covers the mean estimate at 0.905-0.965 in six registered scenarios (target 0.85-0.99); descriptive, not used for the decision; not validated for detectors that are exact functions of the baselines
The omitted-baseline sensitivity analysis gives no false comfort against simulated omitted baselines (V1: gain survives in 98.0% pooled, >= 93.8% per family, when the erasure index is <= 0.5)
The sample-size planner's power predictions hold under its own and a misspecified generator
Increments generalise across datasets or models (formal heterogeneity test)
Construct validity: that the label measures what the evaluator is claimed to measure
